tasks.commitBody:
Mihkel opened the Links page on a phone and found labels floating over nothing: every text input and seven of eight buttons on the page carried no class attribute, and Tailwind's preflight zeroes the native border, background and padding — an unclassed control is invisible. The page's two commits never styled a single control.

The six inputs now carry the roster record-editor idiom verbatim and the buttons its primary/secondary families — matching the app's existing spelling rather than inventing a third.

The piece that outlives the fix is the guard: src/unclassed-controls.spec.ts fails the suite when any input, select, textarea or button in any Svelte source ships without a class — the same four-element family app.css's base rule names — with checkbox/file/radio exempt and the exemption stated. Its scanner is immune to the two failure modes this issue demonstrated in real sweeps — it strips HTML comments before matching (the reported 'unclassed select at InviteSurface:629' was prose inside a comment) and it parses multi-line tags to their real closing bracket (a forward scan that stops at any line ending in '>' truncates at an arrow function and reported twelve already-classed controls as naked — retracted on the issue) — and both immunities are pinned by committed fixture tests against the exported scanner, not by counts over a tree the fix was about to change. The guard demands some class, never a specific one, so the agenda's deliberate border-b-only inline edits pass untouched.

Scope per the retraction (issue comment 5643902977): the Links page is the only surface touched — the body's other named controls were the sweep's artifact, not defects.

Closes #335
